**The public-proof screen (round-5 repair of R4-1; R5-1/R5-2/R5-3).**
Published as `audits/evidence/retrofit/r1-public-proof-screen.py` with its
output `r1-public-proof-screen.out`. *Erratum:* the round-4 run tested
whether a source proof was contained **whole** in its counterpart, but the
round-4 text described "segments ≥ 60 characters". The round-5 auditor ran
the method as described and found six fragment hits that the containment
test could not see. The method below is the one actually run.

- **Method.** Strip comments and all whitespace. Rename each source
  identifier `h` to `f2_h` wherever Catalog declares `f2_h` (dotted names
  split). Report two measures:
  - the **longest common contiguous segment** (LCS), with the literal ≥ 60
    candidate threshold;
  - the **shared length**: greedy string tiling with blocks of at least 25
    characters, as a fraction of the **source** proof.
- **Rule.** A pair is a **member** when at least half of the source proof
  reappears in the target, with an absolute floor of 60 shared characters
  so that a one-line citation of a public lemma counts as reuse. Any other
  shared tiling of at least 60 characters is a recorded **fragment**, not
  counted. The rest are citations or no match.
- **Population (R5-3).** 17 eligible pairs: 2 from Composition (`id`,
  `const`) and **15** from Primitives, not the 16 stated in round 4. Five
  source theorems have no `_spaceUsed` counterpart: `ifEq`, `comp`,
  `splitSolveWith`, `unaryToken`, `appendBit`.
- **Pass 1, direct pairs.**
  - Members (7): `id` 96.5%, `const` 97.1%, `prepend` 93.9%,
    `pairEncodeFixed` 100%, `pairFst`/`pairSnd` 88.8%, `pairConcat`
    88.7%.
  - Fragments, recorded and not counted (3): `polyUnary` (119 characters
    shared, 46.7%); `pairLenCheck` (305, 21.9%; its LCS is the 91-character
    `Nat.pow_one` bound); `stripLast` (221, 11.7%; its LCS is the
    121-character `have hn` weakening).
  - Citations or no match (7): `lengthBits`, `polyBits`, `pairValid`,
    `pairDup`, `pairMapSnd`, `splitSolve` (the auditor's 27-character
    citation), `incFixed`.
  - The literal ≥ 60 LCS screen reproduces the auditor's hit set exactly
    (`id` 776, `const` 273, and 62/75/75/75/91/121 for the six Primitives
    pairs). One member falls below the 60-character LCS threshold:
    `pairEncodeFixed`, whose longest block is 53 characters but whose whole
    91-character source proof reappears. This is why the rule measures
    coverage, not contiguity alone.
- **Pass 2, residual helpers.** Each of the 27 nonmembers recorded in
  round 4 is screened against every public proof of Composition,
  Primitives and TimeConstructible, taking the best match by shared length.
  - Members (2): `f2_strip_linear` (86.0% of `computesFunInTime_stripLast`;
    R5-1) and `f2_counter_heads` (64.1% of `timeConstructible_id`; the
    auditor's 215-character partial-reuse candidate, which crosses the
    member bar once measured by tiling).
  - Fragments, recorded (6): `f2_counter_count_space` 6.5%,
    `f2_unary_sharp` 35.7%, `f2_cond_time` 30.0% (vs
    `bufferedCompTM_computesInTime`, a candidate the auditor did not list),
    `f2_rewind_scan_heads` 7.4%, `f2_rewind_heads` 6.0%,
    `f2_cond_ledger` 11.7%.
  - The remaining 19 share under 60 characters with any public proof.
- **Round-6 repair (R6-1, R6-5): pass 3, exhaustive.** Round 6 found
  R6-1, which the public-only residual pass could not see. Pass 3 replaces
  that scope limit. **Every one of Catalog's 124 non-members** (all of
  Catalog minus the post-R6-1 299-member union, computed by name in the
  script) is screened against **every declaration, public and private, of
  Composition, Primitives, TimeConstructible, Loop and Wrappers** (553
  declarations, of which 542 have an extracted body of at least 25
  characters; the other 11 cannot reach the 60-character floor). An exact 25-character prefilter is used; it loses nothing,
  because every tile is at least 25 characters. Verdicts compare like with
  like, proof with proof and term with term, so a proof that spells out a
  definition's term is reported as a restatement and not counted. **Every**
  qualifying pair is printed, not just each target's best match (R6-5).
  - Result: **19 cross-file members**, all counted in the Catalog row
    above. *Round-7 correction:* the round-6 text derived the source side
    from each target's best match only, giving "6 new source-side members"
    (R7-1). Pass 4 below replaces that hand step.
  - Five A2 members reproduce just over half of one 129-character Loop
    proof, `emLoop_run_prefix`. They are counted, as the rule requires,
    and flagged as low-coverage.
- **Round-7 repair (R7-1, R7-2): pass 4 generates the census.** No
  per-file member count is assembled by hand any more. **Pass 4** runs the
  like-kind rule over **all 423 Catalog declarations**, not only the
  non-members, against all five source files: 537 like-kind MEMBER pairs.
  **Every** pair's source joins its file's member set, together with the
  historical rules, stated by name in the script: f2_-twins, the
  `a2_loop_halted_run` twin, the relocation family, the 13 H3 copies, the
  counter block and `catalog_` twins. The script prints each file's count
  and every member beyond the historical rules, with spans. The rows above
  quote it.
  - Pass 4 reproduces the auditor's R7-1 additions (`controlCfg_run`,
    `emCall_right_run`, `exists_emitLoopTM`).
  - It also finds **24 further source-side members** (Primitives 16, Loop
    7, Wrappers 1). These are source declarations that a Catalog twin of a
    *sibling* declaration reproduces by more than half, so their material
    is duplicated in Catalog. Two of them are Loop's H3 near-copies
    `emLoopHost_init` and `emLoopHost_anchor_return`, previously
    "noted, uncounted"; they are now counted through the cross-file path.
  - Catalog is unchanged at 318.
  - **R7-2:** the body extractor now handles equation-style definitions and
    inductives (text from the first depth-0 `|` or `where`). The population
    labels are exact: 553 source declarations, 542 with an extracted body
    of at least 25 characters; the other 11 are genuinely shorter. Pass 3b
    carries the kind guard: **107 like-kind in-file pairs over 62 targets
    (12 at 90% or more), plus 2 restatements** (`f2_cond_ledger` ~
    `f2_timedReadyCfg`, `a2_loop_prepare` ~ `f2_loopReady`).
- **The membership rule in one sentence.** A declaration is a member when
  it is a historical twin or copy, or when it is either side of a
  like-kind cross-file pair in which at least half of the source's
  extracted body, and at least 60 characters, reappears in the target. The
  **exception** is in-file near-duplicates, which are recorded (pass 3b)
  and not counted; in-file exact copies are counted.
- **Standing in-file convention, stated explicitly.** Pass 3b lists
  in-file near-duplicates among the non-members: **109 raw printed
  pairs, of which 107 are like-kind, over 62 targets**. Twelve like-kind
  pairs reach 90%, and the other 2 are kind-mismatched restatements. They
  are led by the §12 sibling
  machine rows (`transferTM` against `copyTM` 99.8%, and the
  clear/compare/increment rows), which are public constructions audited at
  the §12 and F1 gates. Per the ledger's standing convention, which counts
  in-file **exact** copies (the H3 thirteen, the `a2_mapSumEquiv`/
  `a2_map_sum` pair) and **notes in-file near-duplicates without counting
  them**, they are recorded, not counted. None is an exact copy. Their
  disposition is the 12.2c per-theme split, which factors these families.
  An in-file near-match alone never adds a member. A declaration can still
  be a member independently through a cross-file pair: Loop's
  `emLoopHost_init` and `emLoopHost_anchor_return` count because their
  Catalog twins reproduce them.
- **Coverage qualification.** The screen covers the five source files of
  Catalog's copy families, in full, at the stated thresholds. Copies from
  files outside those families, or adaptations restructured below the
  25-character tile size, are outside it.

Copy-side counts deliberately include copies whose originals were deleted
in R1 (the copies persist; deletion of an original does not shrink the
copy side). The Loop inventory's recorded dispositions — the 8 dead
Loop-twin copies in Catalog (`f2_loop_silent_prefix`,
`f2_loopBody_capture`, the six `f2_loopDebit*`/`f2_loopBorrow*`) and the
orphans' dead twins — are **dispositions for 12.2c, not subtractions
here**; sole-owner/dead labels require Catalog's reference graph and are
settled at that window. Internal near-duplicates flagged by the
inventories but outside the rule (`clCountTape ≡ bufferTape`) are noted,
uncounted. The H3 `_init` pair, once in this list, counts since round 7
through its cross-file Catalog correspondence.

**Epoch R1 delta**: new copies **0**; the historical maps lost **eleven
dead originals plus one live original eliminated by replacement**
(`catalogPair_inverse`, the human-approved E1) — 245 → 233 surviving

**SAT/Hardness adapter debt (gate106 F2; ACKNOWLEDGED by kind by Seyoon, 2026-11-07).**
The acknowledgment covers every re-derivation of the following generic kinds anywhere in
TCSlib, including matching correctness/frame proofs, not merely the currently found sites:

1. **Clean-module contract and its install/emit/stop lifting:** a positive bounded first halt
   from canonical argument tapes, uniform in untouched native input, with prescribed result
   word and emitted output. Canonical current formula is SatClean/CLA5Clean.
2. **Positive-release stop adapter:** add a Boolean release flag so a designated exit becomes
   a halt only after the first source step; preserve physical configuration fields. Includes
   the machine/configuration, step and clean-contract lemmas.
3. **Bank-padding adapter:** embed a k-tape action/configuration/machine into K≥k tapes with
   unused tapes blank, heads0 and stationary actions; includes apply/run/seam commutation.
4. **Finite one-way word transducer:** zero work tapes, parametric finite next/emit/finish/start,
   at most one emission per input plus optional final emission. Includes pure word semantics,
   configuration, run, polynomial-time and head/tail projection proofs.
5. **Polynomial bridge overhead:** len≤A(n+1)^d implies
   c*(A(n+1)^d+n+len+1)+1≤(c*(2*A+1)+1)*(n+1)^(d+1).

`bits_injective`) and the decider wrapper (`arm_decides_poly` on `CA`, the `one_run` case split and
the reject branch). The four languages `validLang`, `initLang`, `acceptLang` and `stepLang`
(Hydroxyi's) already formed 31 copy pairs at the base. The edge-mode PR adds `edgeLang`,
`mem_edgeLang`, `edgeLang_iff` and `edgeLang_mem`, 25 more pairs. About 25 lines of shared text
are the decoding proofs and the wrapper's skeleton. The edge mode's own correctness proof
(`edge_round`, `edge_loop`, `edge_tail`) is in no pair. **Census** (gate 91, minor 3; members of the
family over all declarations, private included): `Langs` 8/9 → 10/12, `Checks` 4/26 → 5/31,
`Deciders` 3/16 → 4/22. `Langs` was already above one fifth at the base, from the four existing
languages; the acceptance above covers it. The edge member crosses no new file's threshold.
**Accepted (user, 2026-11-04)** as debt. **Disposition:** the dedup window (12.2c): one membership
lemma for languages of encoded triples, and one decider wrapper parameterized by the mode's tail,

- **The family, acknowledged by kind for 12.2c (user, 2026-11-05), widened by kind (user,
  2026-11-05):** every proof, anywhere in TCSlib, that one step keeps a configuration within a
  window of any shape (the radius window `Cfg.InWindow`, a per-tape radius, an interval, a
  visited interval), and every proof of window monotonicity. A later find is an accounting minor.
  The canonical statements:
  - `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.apply_iff`: for `c` in the radius-`s` window, `(a.apply c).InWindow s`
    holds iff no work head is at `-s` moving left or at `s` moving right;

  - **the tape half**, to be published in the 12.2c window: an action changes a work cell only
    under that tape's old head (`z ≠ c.workTapePos i → (a.apply c).workTapes i z =
    c.workTapes i z`). It exists today as `TuringMachine/Oracle`'s private
    `apply_workTapes_eq_of_ne` (line 304 at the campaign tip), the natural one to harvest.

## ===== campaign/backlog.md =====

# Backlog

The consolidated tracking file for the Arora-Barak campaign branch
(`complexity/arora-barak-ch1`) and adjacent repository work: human-review
design questions, queued and on-hold campaign work, deferred formalizations,
pending decisions, and housekeeping. Consolidated 2026-09-18 from the two
campaign plans, the audit resolutions records, and session assessments.

**Conventions.** This file is the *canonical home* of the human-review
question statements (§1) — the plans keep stable numbered stubs, since audit
documents cite the numbering — and the *tracking index* for everything else
(scope prose remains in the plans; decision-log history is never moved).
New items land here; an item leaves only by a decision recorded in the
relevant plan's decision log. From the next audit round onward this file
joins the bundle attachment set.

---

## 1. Human-review design questions (reserved — never closed by an automated gate)

Flagged for a **human** auditor/maintainer: the LLM audit rounds verify
correctness, but these are matters of architectural taste and trust-surface
policy.

### CH1-Q1 — the 3A Mathlib-computability bridge

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter1Plan.md` §5 (epoch 3, batch A);
`MathlibBridge.lean`, `Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode`.*

The audited docstring sketch called for the canonizer machine to be
**hand-assembled from this repository's composition combinators** ("its
construction uses the composition combinators", optionally with a polynomial
`canonizerTime`). The delivered proof instead (i) proves the canonization
*function* primitive recursive, (ii) compiles it through **Mathlib's verified
recursion-theory pipeline** (`ToPartrec.Code.exists_code` →
`PartrecToTM2.tr_eval`), (iii) simulates the resulting TM2 stack machine in
our model with a bespoke private `bridgeTM`, and (iv) lands in the binary
alphabet via the proved `alphabet_reduction`, extracting the time bound by
finite maxima (no polynomial bound claimed — permitted, since
`canonizerTime` is existential). The batch flagged the deviation itself; the
maintainer verification pass confirmed the proof is sorry-free with the
standard axiom footprint and zero public-interface drift. **Open questions
for a human:** (a) is the heavyweight `Mathlib.Computability.TMToPartrec`
import into the TM tree acceptable, or should the bridge be quarantined
behind the planned phase-5 `MathlibBridge` module boundary (it effectively
front-runs that module)? (b) is the enlarged trust/review surface (Mathlib's
TM2 semantics + the private `bridgeTM` simulation, ~150 private
declarations) preferable to a longer but self-contained combinator
construction? (c) should the abandoned polynomial-`canonizerTime` claim be
recorded as permanently out of scope, or re-derived later from the
combinator route if one is ever written? Since the epoch-3→4 merge the
bridge lives in the dedicated `MathlibBridge.lean`, which implements the
quarantine that part (a) contemplates — the `TMToPartrec` import is confined
to that one module and nothing outside `exists_effectiveMachineCode` depends
on it — but the implemented quarantine does **not** dispose of this
question: parts (a)-(c) remain open for human review (epoch-4 audit,
finding 3: an earlier version of this text misplaced the bridge inside

### CH1-Q2 — the 3B universal-interpreter proof architecture

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter1Plan.md` §5 (epoch 3, batches B + B2);
`Universal.lean`, `Turing.universal`.*

The proof followed the audited sketch's outline (prefix-only startup,
canonizer capture onto a table tape, four-work-tape interpreter with a fixed
finite controller), but the realized architecture is by far the campaign's
most involved artifact: 2465 lines (2831 after the epoch-4A timed fill), 104
private declarations built across two agent sessions (WIP `f191b918` +
continuation), a bespoke checkpoint relation (`universalRelation`) with
generic block-simulation assembly (`universal_block_run` /
`universal_from_blocks`), a virtual left boundary via a marker tape, a unary
state tape with group-wise table scanning, and an *exact* per-phase cost
ledger realized to `universalBlockBound = 3L + 5N + 20`. The kernel checks
all of it, and the public statement is frozen and audited — but the *design*
was never itself an audit deliverable at this level of detail. **Open
questions for a human:** (a) is this the right load-bearing shape — and
which parts (the capture wrapper, the block-run/`universal_run_join`
assembly, the marker-directed rewind and unary-copy gadget patterns, all
flagged by the agents as promotion candidates) should graduate to shared
modules rather than being re-derived? (b) is the exact-ledger posture
(`3L + 5N + 20` proved to the transition) worth its brittleness against any
future change to `CodeTM.serialize`, or should the maintained invariant be
an existential bound with the exact ledger demoted to documentation? (c)
does the interpreter's claim to *be* the book's universal machine (as
opposed to satisfying the frozen statement, which the kernel settles)
deserve a targeted human read of the construction's core definitions
(`UniversalControl`, `universalInterpreter`, `universalRelation`), given no
executable diagnostics of the whole interpreter ever ran (the batch-B smoke
tests aborted on deep recursion and were discarded)?

*Cross-link: question (b)'s exact ledger is now also load-bearing for the
Chapter-2 `TMSAT_mem_NP` fill (the quantitative public bridge, §2), which
will expose a form of the constant publicly.*

### CH2-Q1 — generality of `HALT_not_mem_NP`

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter2Plan.md` (phase-1, round-2 audit, finding 3);
`ClassNP/Reductions.lean`.*

The statement is currently at `Turing.EffectiveMachineCode` generality
because its proof route reuses Chapter 1's `HALT_not_computable`, whose own
proof runs the universal evaluator. The round-2 auditor showed this
restriction is **not mathematically necessary**: a direct diagonalization —
the public diagonal-pairing machine, the searcher's finite-control transform
with the halt/loop roles swapped, `Turing.exists_codeTM`, no evaluator —
proves `HALT` undecidable for *every* lawful `Turing.MachineCode` (and the
earlier "trivial-machine scheme" counterexample is unlawful: constant
decoding violates `decode_encode`). **The question:** add that diagonal
lemma as a new audited statement (a strengthening of Chapter 1's
uncomputability story that shares its main fill obligation, the
control-transform lemma, with `HALT_NPHard`) and generalize
`HALT_not_mem_NP` to `MachineCode` — or keep the conservative signature as a
documented API/proof-route restriction? Maintainer's provisional choice,
pending review: the conservative signature, with the docstring stating the
restriction honestly; the diagonal lemma is deliberately *not* slipped into
a repair round, since it would enlarge the audited surface of Chapter 1's
uncomputability chapter.

### U-1: re-derive the chapter-1 universal machine from B5a's generic step block (user, 2026-10-11)

*Merged with MIG-2 (user, 2026-10-12): the timed-layer dedup and this re-derivation are one migration item.*

The chapter-1 universal machine (`Turing.universal`, `universal_quadratic`, `timed_universal`) is
a bespoke interpreter of about 5,300 lines across `Universal.lean`, `UniversalStartup.lean`,
`UniversalInterpreter.lean` and `UniversalBlock.lean`. It is hard-wired to one work tape, and it
is already copied once: the timed form carries its own private stopped-interpreter layer. B5a
(`briefs/b5a-fill.md`, design §12.11) builds one format-parameterized interpreter instead. That
is a single private step block for one simulated transition of a `k`-tape coded table, whose
per-round cost is independent of `t` and `x`.

**The item:** after B5a lands, re-derive the three chapter-1 statements from that step block, and
delete the bespoke interpreter layers.

**H1 alone does not suffice.** The frozen statements need what B5a's headline does not give:
- **full output:** `universal` computes `M_α(x)`, and `timed_universal` emits `true :: output`,
  whereas H1 answers only `[true]`/`[false]` from a silent output summary;
- **a per-code linear bound with no `|x|` term:** `universal` is `C(α)·(t + 1)` and
  `timed_universal` is `C(α)·(t + 1)²`, whereas H1 is a polynomial in `|α| + |x| + t`;
- **no deadline, and divergence preserved:** `universal` runs until halt, and its converse says
  every completed output of `U` is one of the simulated machine's.

**Route.** Reuse the step block under new hosts. The natural route is H2 above (the per-code
linear timed simulator, with its suffix-input host), plus an emitting variant of the block's
output handling and an unclocked loop host for `universal`. Keep all three statements unchanged;
`UniversalStartup`'s public input pieces (`universalInput_read`/`_move`) are the suffix-input
host's components.

**Governance.** A 12.2c item: its own PR and gate. The chapter-1 statements are frozen, and every
consumer of `universal`/`timed_universal` is re-checked. Prerequisite: the B5a fill (H1's step
block proved). *Origin: B5a design discussion; user, 2026-10-11.*

### SH-1: retire `Nondeterminism`'s private 2B shell onto W2-V (from the fills-4 integration)

`FinTM.exists_certificateShell` (W2-V, `Build/CertShell.lean`) is proved and admission-free. It
is the public form of the private certificate shell that `ClassNP/Nondeterminism.lean` uses for
`ntime_poly_subset_NP` (`cont_choiceVerifier_mem_P`, its loader, `choiceCore`). Design §12.10,
decision 3, names the deduplication as the shell's second customer, a 12.2c item. W2-V's
`certSplitWord` matches `Nondeterminism`'s private `contSplitWord` at 100% and `e3SplitWord` at
90%. This is one four-line `match` term, the output function of the public
`FinTM.computesFunInTime_splitSolve`, and it was pre-disclosed by W2-V's brief
(`audits/fills-4-integration.md`).

**Scope (corrected 2026-10-12, from the 12.2c readiness check).** W2-V's shell serves only
*polynomial* certificate lengths, so only the polynomial use retires. `Nondeterminism`'s NEXP
route keeps its own exponential search: `e3Split` solves `n + C·2^((n+1)^c) = m`, and its loader
reuses `contPairTM`, which embeds `choiceCore`. **The task, as scoped:** re-derive
`cont_choiceVerifier_mem_P` from `exists_certificateShell` and delete `contSplitWord` with it,
which retires the 100% pair. `e3SplitWord`, `contPairTM` and `choiceCore` stay for the
exponential route. Retiring those too would need a width-parametric public shell: a new
statement, with its own gate, and not worth it for the remaining 90% textual match. Statements
stay unchanged. **Prerequisite:** W2-V's own fill gate (the wave-1 fill gate), so that the cited
shell is audited first. The task gets its own PR and gate.

**Carried (Seyoon, 2026-11-16), after measurement.** The shell's hypothesis needs a plain
machine `P` that reads the input natively and halts by `T (|x| + |u|)` with output `out x u` for
every certificate of the right length. `Nondeterminism`'s `choiceCore` reads `x` from a copied
work tape (it was built for the paired loader), and the public `NDTM.replayTM` does not stop when
the choice word runs out. The public `exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P` is stated for arbitrary `N`, so
no halting hypothesis is available. SH-1 would therefore need a new halting, native-input choice
core with its run lemmas: an estimated +125 to +185 lines against about 100 deleted
(`contSplitWord`, `cont_split_length`, `cont_split_answer`, `cont_split_bridge`,
`choiceVerifier_no_split` and the body of `cont_choiceVerifier_mem_P`). That is about +25 to +85
net, to retire one 4-line pair. Revisit only if a native-input bounded replay core is published
for another consumer.

  - (b) At every Lean or Mathlib bump, remove the names in `TCSlib/Programs/Compat.lean` that the
    bump provides, and revisit the `with_unfolding_none` to `with_reducible` swap.
  - (c) The extensions are a statement phase with its gate: reading the input in place, `emit`, and
    the coin stream for nondeterminism and randomization. **Semantics decided** (user,
    2026-10-12; design §15c): now **PROG-2**.
  - (d) Stage 2, the RAM-to-`FinTM` simulation.

    stage 2 need them (fidelity gate, finding 3). Both are generic, and outside the vendored
    closure.

* **PROG-2: the extension edit set** (user, 2026-10-12; design §15c). All four extensions in one
  scripted vendored edit set:
  - `inBit`/`inLen` with a RAM `rdIn` (`len` only if needed);
  - `emit`, with an append-only output;
  - read-once coins (`coin x`);
  - `half`, as a statement and a RAM shift.

  I/O and coins become indices of `Exec`, so `Ends`, `Meets` and the routines are unchanged; a new
  `EndsIO` sees them. Also part of the set:
  - the `Exec` determinism lemma, which randomized acceptance needs;
  - `Fits`'s input-length clause;
  - an update to `ComputationalModels.lean`'s instruction-count docstring.

  **Estimate:** 600–1,000 vendored lines, by `scripts/vendor_afm26/`, plus 700–1,150 new.
  **Gate:** a fidelity check of the vendored edits, then a statement gate for the new rules.
  **Obligation from the stage-2 gate (F3):** the edited compiler must supply `1 ≤ lim.word` at the
  existing simulation calls (`Compiler/Simulation.lean:277`, `:356`), as an invariant or a
  premise; it does not follow from `input_le`.

* **PROG-3: memory footprint along a run** (from the PROG-2 survey; design §15c, obstacle 1).
  `compileProgram_correct` describes only the final memory. Stage 2's space bound needs every
  intermediate memory inside `[-lowCell, lim.space)`. Close it with a stronger `Steps` or by
  porting `Machine/Footprint.lean` (PROG-1(e)). It is a prerequisite for stage 2's space bound,
  and so for L, Savitch and PSPACE through programs, and for C2's log-space programs (design
  §16b item 4).

* **PROG-4: stage 2's statement requirements** (user, 2026-10-12; design §16b items 1 and 4).
  Stage 2 (PROG-1(d)) is drafted together with PROG-2 and PROG-3, and its statement carries:
  - **a computed word size:** `W` is a function of the input length that the compiled machine
    computes within its space bound (`c·log n` for P and L, `c·S(n)` for Savitch);
  - **deterministic and nondeterministic forms:** each `coin` one `FinNDTM` choice step, with
    bounds uniform over the coin streams;

* **Relativized hierarchy theorems** ([AB09] §3.4, remark: the hierarchy proofs relativize). **Deferred (Seyoon, 2026-11-16)** until after the chapters 3–4 closeout, possibly after integration into `main`. Starting point: `campaign/closeout/W9-DESIGN.md` (one model-generic interface for the three hierarchy proofs; the oracle instances need a universal oracle machine, oracle codes, an oracle clocked runner and an oracle space class, 30–40k lines for all three; proposed oracle space convention: count the query tape). *Origin: closeout plan D3/W9.*
* **B5a linear headline (formerly "B5a headline H2", renamed 2026-10-13 to avoid confusion with host H2): the per-code-linear timed simulator** (user, 2026-10-11:
  "H1 for now, but add H2 to backlog"). `CodeSimulator.lean`'s headline is
  H1, polynomial in `|α| + |x| + t` jointly, which is exactly what the two
  uniform schemes need. **H2** gives the same verdicts within
  `d · (|α| + 1)^d · (t + 1)`, with no `|x|` term and linear in `t` per
  code. It would make the one interpreter the stage-1 timed universal at
  linear overhead. It needs a **suffix-input host**: the simulated machine
  reads `x` in place inside the native input, behind a left-boundary
  marker. The pieces are public (`universalInput_read`/`_move`,
  `UniversalStartup.lean`), but no host composes them. H2 ⇒ H1 is already
  proved (`exists_uniformSimulator_of_timed`, B5a statement probe), so H2
  can later be added beside H1 without disturbing its consumers. The step
  block's per-round cost is independent of `t` and `x`, so the B5a fill's
  trace is the H2 core. H2 is also the natural route for 12.2c item **U-1** (§1).
  *Origin: B5a dossier D3; design §12.11.*

### Chapter 6 (Arora–Barak §§6.1–6.5): what is proved, and what remains

The machine-facing Chapter-6 bridge theorems this section used to list are all
**proved, sorry-free** (headline `#print axioms`: `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
`Quot.sound` only), over the book's DAG model `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit`:

* Thm 6.6 `P ⊆ P/poly` — `Complexity.P_subset_PPoly` (oblivious tableau,
  `CircuitComplexity/PSubsetPPoly*.lean`); `P ⊊ P/poly` (p. 110) —
  `Complexity.P_ssubset_PPoly`, with the machine-model `UHALT`
  (`Complexity.UHALT_not_mem_P`, `UHaltMachine.lean`).
* Lem 6.10 / 6.11 — `BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_NPComplete`,
  `BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_polyTimeReducible_SAT3`, and Cook–Levin via circuits
  `Complexity.SAT3_NPHard_viaCircuits` (the p. 111 alternative proof); CKT-SAT `∈ NP` is
  `BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_mem_NP`, circuit evaluation `BoolCircuit.CVAL_mem_P`.
* Remark 6.7, Thm 6.13 — `Complexity.tabFamily_isPUniform`,
  `Language.mem_P_iff_exists_isPUniform`; Def 6.14, Thm 6.15 and the logspace half of
  Remark 6.7 — `Complexity.tabFamily_isLogspaceUniform`,
  `Language.mem_P_iff_exists_isLogspaceUniform`.
* Def 6.16, Ex 6.17, Thm 6.18 — `Complexity.DTIMEAdvice`,
  `Complexity.mem_PAdvicePoly_of_le_allOnes` (with the named `UHALT` instances
  `Complexity.UHALT_mem_DTIMEAdvice_one`, `Complexity.UHALT_mem_PAdvicePoly`),
  `Complexity.PPoly_eq_PAdvicePoly`, and the book's advice length `n^d` literally:
  `Complexity.PPoly_eq_iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_pow` (`P/poly = ⋃ DTIME(n^c + 1)/n^d`,
  `PAdviceSubsetPPoly.lean`). The time `n^c + 1` is forced, not cosmetic: the literal
  `DTIME(n^c)/a` is empty for `c ≥ 1` (`Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq_empty`, zero steps
  on the empty input), so the literal union collapses to constant time
  (`Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq`); also
  `DTIME(T)/0 = DTIME(T)` for `T(n) ≥ n + 1` (`Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_DTIME`)
  and `⋃_c DTIME(n^c + 1)/0 = P` (`Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_P`).
* Thm 6.19 Karp–Lipton — `Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_subset_PPoly`; Thm 6.20
  Meyer — `Complexity.EXP_eq_SigmaP_two_of_EXP_subset_PPoly`, and the p. 115 corollary
  `Complexity.not_EXP_subset_PPoly_of_P_eq_NP`.
* Thm 6.21 — `BoolCircuit.exists_hard_function_dag` (book bound `2ⁿ/(10n)`), with the
  p. 115 probabilistic form `BoolCircuit.prob_computableDAG_shannon_le`, proved by the
  book's steps: `BoolCircuit.prob_eval_eq_apply` (`Pr[C(x) = f(x)] = 1/2`),
  `BoolCircuit.prob_computes` / `prob_computes_eq_prod` (`Pr[C computes f] = 2^{-2ⁿ}`, the
  product of the per-input probabilities) and the union bound `BoolCircuit.prob_computableDAG_le_count`
  (`ShannonProbabilistic.lean`).
* p. 108 circuit remarks — Lupanov `O(2ⁿ/n)` (`BoolCircuit.exists_dagCircuit_faninTwo_size_le_div`,
  `Lupanov.lean`); fan-out two (`DAGCircuit.exists_fanoutTwo`, `FanOut.lean`), including
  `¬¬v` buffers under the literal fan-in-exactly-two convention
  (`DAGCircuit.exists_fanoutTwo_notNot`, `5S`; `DAGCircuit.IsStrict.exists_fanoutTwo`,
  `20S`; `StrictFanOut.lean`); the literal Def 6.1 (`DAGCircuit.IsStrict`,
  `Language.inPPoly_iff_inStrictPPoly`); formulas as fan-out-one circuits, both ways
  (`TreeCircuit.toDAG_fanout_le_one`, `DAGCircuit.exists_treeCircuit_of_fanout_le_one`,
  `FormulaFanOut.lean`).
* Def 6.5's literal `⋃_c SIZE(n^c)` — empty (`Language.not_inSIZE_pow`); `P/poly` is the
  literal bound from length 2 on (`Language.inPPoly_iff_eventually`, `PPoly.lean`).

Remaining Chapter-6 items (each documented as a divergence in its file):

* **Thm 6.22, the size hierarchy over the book's `SIZE`** — only the tree-circuit
  analogue exists (`BoolCircuit.treeSize_ssubset`, `Hierarchy.lean`); the DAG version
  needs a DAG-native padding/counting argument on top of `exists_hard_function_dag`.
* **Tree-circuit CKT-SAT** (`Encoding.lean`, `CircuitSat.lean`) carries no `≤ₚ` claim —
  only equisatisfiability and a clause count; the book's Lem 6.11 is the DAG version
  above.
* The `O(T log T)` oblivious simulation (Remark 1.7) is Chapter 1's Phase 5 above; the
  circuits of `P ⊆ P/poly` are quadratic instead, which suffices for every Chapter-6 use.

```
/-

import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeFormat
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CounterLoop
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Seam
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.VirtualInput
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.StepBlock
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.StepBlockLoop
-- B5a continuation: sanctioned imports for the physical binary-header loader.
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputCall
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputRewind
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Nondeterministic
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InterpreterStartup

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The uniform code simulator

One format-parameterized simulator for deterministic machine codes: on
`⟨⟨bits t, α⟩, x⟩` it decides whether the machine that `α` denotes halts on `x`
with output exactly `[true]` within `t` steps, in time **one polynomial in
`|α| + |x| + t + 1` jointly**. The parameter is a `Turing.MachineFormat`: a
`Turing.CodeFormat` (12.2c item 8's parse layer) whose codes denote `k`-work-tape
binary machines in the fixed `k`-record serialization. The one-work-tape codes
(`Turing.oneTapeMachineFormat`) and the two-work-tape codes of `Codes2Tape` are
instances; they supply `Turing.exists_uniformMachineCode` (`Diagonalization/EXPCOM`)
and `Turing.exists_uniformMachineCode2` (`Codes2Tape`). [AB09, §1.4.1, Theorem 1.9;
the uniform form required by Example 3.6(3), audited at phase P3.2 round 2]

## Design

* **One interpreter, parameterized by the record grammar.** The table of a
  `k`-tape code is `3^(k+1)` `Turing.actionBitsK` records per state
  (`Turing.tableBitsK`); a single finite machine per format interprets it.
* **Canonize first, then interpret.** The decoded machine's serialization is
  computed in polynomial time (`Turing.MachineFormat.exists_polyCanonizer`):
  the binary state count and the minimum-length guard are checked before any
  state-indexed work, so a huge declared count is never expanded in unary.
* **The clock is §12.7's counter loop** (`Turing.counterLoopTM`) over the
  deadline's binary word; a simulated halt is a live body exit.
* **Status.** The canonizer `Turing.MachineFormat.exists_polyCanonizer` is proved, with
  no admission. A validator (`exists_canonDecider`) runs the two-port parse front end
  (`exists_canonParseFront`: header validity, canonicality and the binary length guard) and
  the grammar stage (`exists_canonGrammarStage`) on one bank and emits one verdict bit; the
  strip machine (`exists_canonStripTM`) or the constant fallback follows. The grammar stage
  checks the unary initial state against the header (the bounded unary reader
  `exists_canonUnaryTM`), runs two nested public counter loops, over `n + 1` states and
  `3^(k+1)` records each, on the fresh-anchor record round (`canonReturnAdapter` around the
  record validator `exists_canonRecordTM`), and tests the all-`true` suffix; its time is
  quadratic in the input length and independent of the header's value.
  The uniform simulator `Turing.MachineFormat.exists_uniformSimulator` is proved, with no
  admission: the interpreter startup (`Turing.exists_interpreterStartup`, with the canonizer
  installed) seamed to the binary deadline clock around the complete generic step block
  `Turing.StepBlock.roundTM` of `Build/StepBlock`, hosted on the virtual input, with its one-bit
  verdict (`h1HostedVerdict_accepts`), the clock being the public loop
  `Turing.StepBlock.hostedLoopTM_run` of `Build/StepBlockLoop`.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.serializeK`, `Turing.codeSkipTableK` — the fixed `k`-record serialization
  and grammar, over the table layout `Turing.workReadsK`, `Turing.tableBitsK` of
  `Build/StepBlock`.
* `Turing.serializeK_eq` — the serialization as an equation, the specification API (user,
  2026-10-16).
* `Turing.MachineFormat`, `Turing.MachineFormat.toFinTM` — the format parameter.
* `Turing.oneTapeMachineFormat` — the one-work-tape instance.

## Main results

* `Turing.tableBitsK_two`, `Turing.codeSkipTable2_eq_codeSkipTableK` — the
  two-work-tape bridges to `CodeFormat`'s frozen table writer and skipper.
* `Turing.MachineFormat.exists_polyCanonizer` — a polynomial-time canonizer.
* `Turing.MachineFormat.exists_uniformSimulator` — the uniform simulator.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4, §1.4.1, Theorem 1.9; Example 3.6(3).)
-/

namespace Turing

/-! ## The `k`-record layout -/

/-- The canonical serialization of a `k`-work-tape binary machine with `n + 1`
states: the binary state count, the unary initial state, the table. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def serializeK {k n : ℕ} (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode n.bits (unaryFin M.q₀ ++ tableBitsK M.tr)

/-- **The serialization as an equation** (the specification API, user 2026-10-16): the doubled
binary state count, the separator, the unary initial state, then the table. Consumers read the
captured serialization through this equation (with `Turing.pairEncode_eq` and
`Turing.unaryFin_eq`), not by unfolding `Turing.serializeK`. -/
theorem serializeK_eq {k n : ℕ} (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    serializeK M = pairEncode n.bits (unaryFin M.q₀ ++ tableBitsK M.tr) :=
  rfl

/-- The table skipper of the `k`-record grammar: `n + 1` states of `3^(k+1)`
records each. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipTableK (k n : ℕ) : List Bool → Option (List Bool) :=
  codeSkipRepeat ((fun r => codeSkipRepeat r 3)^[k + 1] (codeSkipActionK k n)) (n + 1)

/-- A one-tape read vector built by `Fin.cons` is the constant function. -/
private lemma fin_cons_one (w : Option Bool) :
    (Fin.cons w Fin.elim0 : Fin 1 → Option Bool) = fun _ => w := by
  funext i; fin_cases i; rfl

/-- A two-tape read vector built by `Fin.cons` is the `Turing.workPair` of its entries. -/
private lemma fin_cons_two (w₀ w₁ : Option Bool) :
    (Fin.cons w₀ (fun _ : Fin 1 => w₁) : Fin 2 → Option Bool) = workPair w₀ w₁ := by
  funext i; fin_cases i <;> rfl

/-- The one-work-tape reads are the constant functions, in table order. -/
lemma workReadsK_one : workReadsK 1 =
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).map fun w => fun _ => w := by
  simp [workReadsK, fin_cons_one]

/-- The two-work-tape reads are the `Turing.workPair`s, in table order. -/
lemma workReadsK_two : workReadsK 2 =
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).map fun w₁ => workPair w₀ w₁ := by
  simp [workReadsK, fin_cons_one, fin_cons_two]

/-- At two work tapes the generic table writer is `Turing.codeTable2Bits`. -/
lemma tableBitsK_two {n : ℕ}
    (tr : Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → (Fin 2 → Option Bool) → Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    tableBitsK tr = codeTable2Bits (fun q inp w₀ w₁ => tr q inp (workPair w₀ w₁)) := by
  unfold tableBitsK codeTable2Bits
  rw [workReadsK_two]
  simp only [List.flatMap_assoc, List.flatMap_map]

/-- At two work tapes the generic table skipper is `Turing.codeSkipTable2`. -/
lemma codeSkipTable2_eq_codeSkipTableK (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeSkipTable2 n xs = codeSkipTableK 2 n xs := rfl

/-! ## Machine formats -/

/-- A **deterministic machine format**: a `Turing.CodeFormat` whose codes denote
`k`-work-tape binary machines, serialized in the fixed `k`-record layout and
parsed by the fixed `k`-record grammar. [AB09, §1.4] -/
structure MachineFormat extends CodeFormat where
  /-- the work-tape count of the coded machines -/
  k : ℕ
  /-- the machine a code denotes -/
  machine : (M : Code) → MultiTapeTM k Bool (Fin (numStates M + 1))
  /-- the format's serialization is the fixed `k`-record serialization -/
  serialize_eq : ∀ M, serialize M = serializeK (machine M)
  /-- the format's table skipper is the fixed `k`-record skipper -/
  skipTable_eq : ∀ n xs, skipTable n xs = codeSkipTableK k n xs

/-- The bundled machine a code of a machine format denotes. -/
def MachineFormat.toFinTM (F : MachineFormat) (M : F.Code) : FinTM Bool where
  k := F.k
  State := Fin (F.numStates M + 1)
  tm := F.machine M

/-- The one-tape format's table skipper is the generic skipper at one work tape: the
framed one-tape action skipper is `Turing.codeSkipActionK 1`. -/
private lemma oneTape_skipTable_eq (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    oneTapeFormat.skipTable n xs = codeSkipTableK 1 n xs := by
  have h : codeSkipAction n = codeSkipActionK 1 n :=
    funext (codeSkipAction_eq_codeSkipActionK n)
  show codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipAction n) 3) 3) (n + 1) xs = _
  rw [h]; rfl

/-- The frozen one-tape serialization is the generic one at one work tape, record for
record (`Turing.workReadsK_one`, `Turing.actionBits_eq_actionBitsK`). -/
private lemma oneTape_serialize_eq (M : CodeTM) : M.serialize = serializeK M.tm := by
  unfold CodeTM.serialize serializeK tableBitsK
  rw [workReadsK_one]
  simp only [List.flatMap_map, actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]

/-- The one-work-tape code format `Turing.oneTapeFormat` as a machine format.
Its decoder is `Turing.codeDecode` and its bundled machines are
`Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM`, both definitionally. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def oneTapeMachineFormat : MachineFormat :=
  { oneTapeFormat with
    k := 1
    machine := fun M => M.tm
    serialize_eq := oneTape_serialize_eq
    skipTable_eq := oneTape_skipTable_eq }

namespace MachineFormat

variable (F : MachineFormat)

/-! ### Positive grammar bound (B5a fill preparation)

These lemmas justify the extra fail-fast guard even when `F.guard = 0`.
They concern the specified parser; the finite binary implementation and its
polynomial time ledger remain the canonizer's continuation obligation.
-/

/-- Iterated skipping consumes the sum of the per-record lower bounds.

**Proof sketch.** Split off the first successful skip, apply the induction
hypothesis to its suffix, and add the two length inequalities. -/
private lemma skipRepeat_consumes (r : List Bool → Option (List Bool)) (b : ℕ)
    (hr : ∀ xs ys, r xs = some ys → b + ys.length ≤ xs.length)
    (m : ℕ) (xs ys : List Bool) (h : codeSkipRepeat r m xs = some ys) :
    b * m + ys.length ≤ xs.length := by
  induction m generalizing xs with
  | zero =>
    have heq : xs = ys := Option.some.inj h
    simp [heq]
  | succ m ih =>
    obtain ⟨zs, hz, hy⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp h
    have hfirst := hr xs zs hz
    have hrest := ih zs hy
    rw [Nat.mul_succ]
    omega

/-- Nesting a three-symbol reader multiplies its consumption bound by three. -/
private lemma skipSymbols_consumes (r : List Bool → Option (List Bool)) (b : ℕ)
    (hr : ∀ xs ys, r xs = some ys → b + ys.length ≤ xs.length)
    (j : ℕ) (xs ys : List Bool)
    (h : ((fun f => codeSkipRepeat f 3)^[j] r) xs = some ys) :
    b * 3 ^ j + ys.length ≤ xs.length := by
  induction j generalizing xs ys with
  | zero => simpa using hr xs ys h
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply'] at h
    have hb := skipRepeat_consumes _ (b * 3 ^ j) (fun u v huv => ih u v huv)
      3 xs ys h
    simpa only [Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_assoc] using hb

/-- A successful table skip consumes a positive number of bits per state,
independently of the format's optional guard. -/
private lemma skipTable_consumes (k n : ℕ) (xs ys : List Bool)
    (h : codeSkipTableK k n xs = some ys) :
    (4 * k + 5) * 3 ^ (k + 1) * (n + 1) + ys.length ≤ xs.length := by
  have ha (u v : List Bool) (hu : codeSkipActionK k n u = some v) :
      4 * k + 5 + v.length ≤ u.length := by
    rw [← codeEraseActionK] at hu
    obtain ⟨⟨a, rest⟩, hread, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.mp hu
    rw [codeReadActionK_sound u a rest hread, List.length_append]
    exact Nat.add_le_add_right (codeActionK_length a) _
  exact skipRepeat_consumes _ _ (fun u v huv =>
    skipSymbols_consumes _ _ ha (k + 1) u v huv) (n + 1) xs ys h

/-- A successful scanner satisfies the positive grammar guard already on the
suffix following the binary header. This holds also for a zero format guard.

**Proof sketch.** Decompose the successful scanner into its header, initial-state
and table checks. Erasure and initial-state reader soundness show that the table
input is a suffix of the header remainder. Apply the generic table-skip bound
and discard the nonnegative final-suffix length. -/
private lemma scan_grammar_guard (α bits rest tail : List Bool)
    (hp : pairDecode α = some (bits, rest)) (hs : F.scan α = some tail) :
    (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (codeBitsNat bits + 1) ≤ rest.length := by
  unfold CodeFormat.scan at hs
  rw [hp] at hs
  dsimp only [bind, Option.bind] at hs
  split at hs
  · contradiction
  split at hs
  · contradiction
  obtain ⟨table, hq, ht⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp hs
  obtain ⟨suffix, htable, _⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp ht
  rw [F.skipTable_eq] at htable
  have hlen := skipTable_consumes F.k (codeBitsNat bits) table suffix htable
  rw [← codeEraseFin] at hq
  obtain ⟨⟨q, r⟩, hread, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.mp hq
  have hword := codeReadFin_sound rest q r hread
  have hrest : r.length ≤ rest.length := by
    rw [hword, List.length_append]
    omega
  dsimp only at hlen
  omega

/-- Reject a binary header whose declared table cannot fit in the remaining
input, before evaluating the format scanner. This is a specification function,
not yet a certified finite-machine implementation. -/
private def guardedScan (α : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) := do
  let (bits, rest) ← pairDecode α
  if rest.length < (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (codeBitsNat bits + 1)
    then none else F.scan α

/-- The additional positive guard preserves the scanner exactly.

**Proof sketch.** Header failure already fails the scanner. If the new guard
fails, any hypothetical successful scan contradicts `scan_grammar_guard`;
otherwise the guarded scanner calls the original scanner. -/
private lemma guardedScan_eq (α : List Bool) : guardedScan F α = F.scan α := by
  unfold guardedScan
  cases hp : pairDecode α with
  | none => simp [CodeFormat.scan, hp]
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨bits, rest⟩
    dsimp only [bind, Option.bind]
    split
    next hg =>
      cases hs : F.scan α with
      | none => rfl
      | some tail =>
        have := scan_grammar_guard F α bits rest tail hp hs
        omega
    · rfl

/-- Early failure of the positive grammar guard selects exactly the prescribed
fallback, including for a zero guard and a potentially accepting fallback. -/
private lemma decode_of_grammar_guard (α bits rest : List Bool)
    (hp : pairDecode α = some (bits, rest))
    (hg : rest.length < (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (codeBitsNat bits + 1)) :
    F.decode α = F.fallback := by
  have hs : F.scan α = none := by
    rw [← guardedScan_eq]
    simp [guardedScan, hp, hg]
  have hparse : F.parseFull α = none := by
    rw [F.scan_full] at hs
    exact Option.map_eq_none_iff.mp hs
  exact F.decode_of_parseFull_none α hparse

/-- Passing the positive guard bounds state-count work by the available input. -/
private lemma grammar_guard_states (n s : ℕ)
    (h : (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (n + 1) ≤ s) : n + 1 ≤ s := by
  have hc : 1 ≤ (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) :=
    Nat.mul_pos (by omega) (Nat.pow_pos (by omega))
  have hs : n + 1 ≤ (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (n + 1) := by
    simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul_right (n + 1) hc
  exact hs.trans h

/-! ### Physical binary-header loading (B5a continuation) -/

/-- The undoubled header, or the empty word when the pair grammar fails.
The later validation phase must distinguish failure from a valid zero header. -/
private def canonHeader (α : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  ((pairDecode α).map Prod.fst).getD []

/-- Loading a doubled header never produces more bits than the source input. -/
private lemma canonHeader_length (α : List Bool) : (canonHeader α).length ≤ α.length := by
  cases hp : pairDecode α with
  | none => simp [canonHeader, hp]
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨bits, rest⟩
    have he := congrArg List.length (eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode α bits rest hp)
    rw [length_pairEncode] at he
    simp only [canonHeader, hp, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]
    omega

/-- A physical linear-time header loader installs the binary header on tape
zero and restores a clean seam with the original native input available.

**Proof sketch.** Install the public pair-first extractor through the public
native-input call row. The header length is at most the original input length,
so the call row's ledger is linear as well. No parsing or host trace is copied. -/
private lemma exists_canonHeaderCall :
    ∃ (C : FinTM Bool) (entry exit : C.State) (a : ℕ), 0 < C.k ∧
      ∀ α : List Bool, ∃ t ≤ a * (α.length + 1), 0 < t ∧
        (∀ u, 0 < u → u < t →
          (C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) entry (fun _ => [])) u).state ≠
            some exit) ∧
        C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) entry (fun _ => [])) t =
          Cfg.ofWords exit (stateWord C.k (canonHeader α)) := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst
  obtain ⟨C, entry, exit, c, hk, hC⟩ :=
    FinTM.exists_inputCallTM M canonHeader (fun n => a * (n + 1)) hM
  refine ⟨C, entry, exit, c * (a + 2), hk, ?_⟩
  intro α
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hpos, hcut, hrun⟩ := hC α
  refine ⟨t, ht.trans ?_, hpos, hcut, hrun⟩
  have hlen := canonHeader_length α
  calc
    c * (a * (α.length + 1) + α.length + (canonHeader α).length + 1) ≤
        c * (a * (α.length + 1) + 2 * (α.length + 1)) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (by omega)
    _ = _ := by ring

/-! ### Physical fail-fast length guard (B5a continuation)

The catalog has whole-input scans but no fixed-block input scan with a short-input
exit. The following body supplies that missing finite controller; the binary
countdown itself is the public `counterLoopTM`, not a new loop implementation.
The body has no work tapes and never emits. Its block length is `b + 1`, so
even the zero-format-guard case can use the positive grammar minimum.
-/

/-- Progress through a fixed positive block; `none` is the short-input exit. -/
private def guardPhase (b u : ℕ) : Option (Fin (b + 1)) :=
  some ⟨u % (b + 1), Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.succ_pos _)⟩

/-- Read at most `b + 1` actual input symbols, returning to the anchor after
one whole block and taking a distinct live exit on a boundary blank. -/
private def guardBlockTM (b : ℕ) : MultiTapeTM 0 Bool (Option (Fin (b + 1))) where
  q₀ := guardPhase b 0
  tr := fun q inp _ => match q with
    | none => inputMoveAction 0 none
    | some i => if inp.isSome then
        inputMoveAction 1 (guardPhase b (i.val + 1))
      else inputMoveAction 0 none

/-- A block-scan configuration after `j` input cells have been consumed. -/
private def guardCfg (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (q : Option (Fin (b + 1)))
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) :
    Cfg 0 Bool (Option (Fin (b + 1))) x :=
  ⟨some q, ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩, Fin.elim0, Fin.elim0, out⟩

/-- The finite block controller advances one cell without writing or emitting.
The input-only action law supplies all unchanged configuration fields. -/
private lemma guardBlock_step (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (u j : ℕ)
    (hu : u < b + 1) (hj : j < x.length) (out : List Bool) :
    (guardBlockTM b).step (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out) =
      guardCfg b x (guardPhase b (u + 1)) (j + 1) (by omega) out := by
  have hr := inputSymbolInner
    (cfg := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out) j (by dsimp [guardCfg]; omega) hj
  rw [step_of_inputMoveAction (guardBlockTM b) _ (q' := guardPhase b (u + 1)) 1 rfl (by
    change (if (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out).inputSymbol.isSome then
      inputMoveAction 1 (guardPhase b (u % (b + 1) + 1)) else inputMoveAction 0 none) = _
    rw [hr]
    simp only [Option.isSome_some, if_true, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hu])]
  apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
  · rfl
  · apply Fin.ext
    change (moveInputPos (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out).inputPos
      SignType.pos).val = j + 1 + 1
    rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by dsimp [guardCfg]; omega)]
    rfl
  · rfl

/-- Every available prefix of one block is traversed in exactly its length.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the traversed prefix and apply the input-only
one-step contract. The upper bound prevents an intermediate anchor return. -/
private lemma guardBlock_run (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) (u : ℕ)
    (hu : u ≤ b + 1) (hlen : j + u ≤ x.length) :
    (guardBlockTM b).runFrom (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) u =
      guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) (j + u) hlen out := by
  induction u with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ u ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (by omega) (by omega)]
    simpa only [Nat.add_assoc] using
      guardBlock_step b x u (j + u) (by omega) (by omega) out

/-- At the right input blank, the next transition takes the short-input exit. -/
private lemma guardBlock_blank (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (u : ℕ) (out : List Bool) :
    (guardBlockTM b).step
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) x.length le_rfl out) =
      guardCfg b x none x.length le_rfl out := by
  rw [step_of_inputMoveAction (guardBlockTM b) _ (q' := none) 0 rfl (by
    simp [guardBlockTM, guardPhase, Cfg.inputSymbol, guardCfg])]
  simp only [moveInputPos_zero]
  rfl

/-- A short block exits immediately after reading its remaining symbols.
In particular the running time does not depend on the declared state count. -/
private lemma guardBlock_short (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (hshort : x.length - j < b + 1) (out : List Bool) :
    (guardBlockTM b).runFrom (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out)
        (x.length - j + 1) = guardCfg b x none x.length le_rfl out := by
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step',
    guardBlock_run b x j hj out (x.length - j) (by omega) (by omega)]
  have hpos : j + (x.length - j) = x.length := by omega
  simpa only [hpos] using guardBlock_blank b x (x.length - j) out

/-- Exact duration of a block: its fixed size, or the available suffix plus
one transition detecting the blank, whichever is smaller. -/
private def guardTime (b : ℕ) {x : List Bool}
    (c : Cfg 0 Bool (Option (Fin (b + 1))) x) : ℕ :=
  min (b + 1) (x.length + 2 - c.inputPos.val)

/-- Before the end of a block, neither live exit has been reached.

**Proof sketch.** Every strict-interior time is smaller than the block size
and traverses only existing input cells. Its progress index is strictly
positive and below the modulus, so it is neither the anchor nor the failure. -/
private lemma guardBlock_interior (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) (u : ℕ) (hu : 0 < u)
    (ht : u < guardTime b (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out)) :
    ∃ s, ((guardBlockTM b).runFrom
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) u).state = some s ∧
      s ≠ guardPhase b 0 ∧ s ≠ none := by
  have hb : u < b + 1 := lt_of_lt_of_le ht (Nat.min_le_left _ _)
  have hl : j + u ≤ x.length := by
    have := lt_of_lt_of_le ht (Nat.min_le_right _ _)
    dsimp [guardCfg] at this
    omega
  rw [guardBlock_run b x j hj out u (by omega) hl]
  refine ⟨guardPhase b u, rfl, ?_, Option.some_ne_none _⟩
  intro he
  have hv := congrArg (fun q => q.map Fin.val) he
  simp [guardPhase, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hb] at hv
  omega

/-- The physical binary guard is the shared counter loop with the block
controller as body. It has exactly one work tape, holding the binary count. -/
private def binaryGuardTM (b : ℕ) :
    MultiTapeTM 1 Bool (CounterLoopState (Option (Fin (b + 1)))) :=
  counterLoopTM (guardBlockTM b) (guardPhase b 0) (some none)

/-- Guard entry with the binary counter delimited at the origin. The original
input remains native, so the caller can rewind and parse it after the guard. -/
private def binaryGuardStart (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out w : List Bool) :
    Cfg 1 Bool (CounterLoopState (Option (Fin (b + 1)))) x :=
  counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run))
    (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) (FinTM.bufferTape w) 0

/-- While whole blocks fit, the body orbit advances by their combined length.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the number of blocks. The next full block takes
`b + 1` transitions by `guardBlock_run`, returns its finite progress index to
zero, and preserves the output. This is a body-orbit calculation; the physical
counter is handled solely by the public counter-loop contracts. -/
private lemma guardBlock_orbit (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length) :
    counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b)
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) r =
      guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) hr out := by
  induction r with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ r ih =>
    have hprev : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length := by
      rw [Nat.mul_succ] at hr
      omega
    change (fun c => (guardBlockTM b).runFrom c (guardTime b c))^[r + 1] _ = _
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    change (guardBlockTM b).runFrom
      (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b)
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) r)
      (guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b)
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) r)) = _
    rw [ih hprev]
    have ht : guardTime b
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) hprev out) = b + 1 := by
      dsimp [guardTime, guardCfg]
      rw [Nat.min_eq_left]
      rw [Nat.mul_succ] at hr
      omega
    rw [ht, guardBlock_run b x _ hprev out (b + 1) le_rfl (by
      rw [Nat.mul_succ] at hr
      omega)]
    simp only [guardPhase, Nat.mod_self, Nat.zero_mod, Nat.mul_succ, Nat.add_assoc]

/-- Each block is a positive first-return-or-exit segment, including an empty
suffix. This is the hypothesis shared by the returning and escaping host rows. -/
private lemma guardBlock_segment (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) :
    let c := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out
    c.state = some (guardPhase b 0) ∧ 0 < guardTime b c ∧
      (∀ u, 0 < u → u < guardTime b c →
        ∃ s, ((guardBlockTM b).runFrom c u).state = some s ∧
          s ≠ guardPhase b 0 ∧ s ≠ none) := by
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_, guardBlock_interior b x j hj out⟩
  dsimp [guardTime, guardCfg]
  omega

/-- If the requested whole blocks fit, the physical guard reaches `done`,
silently, in linear time in the input length and the binary counter width.

**Proof sketch.** The body orbit supplies the counter host's first-return
hypotheses. Its exact run is the existing `counterLoopTM_run_done`; its
ledger is `counterLoop_time_le`. Both the number of rounds and their total
input consumption are bounded by the actual input length. -/
private lemma binaryGuard_done (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out w : List Bool)
    (hfit : j + (b + 1) * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) ≤ x.length) :
    ∃ T ≤ 5 * x.length + 2 * w.length + 2,
      let c := (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T
      c.state = some .done ∧ c.output = out ∧
        c.inputPos.val = j + (b + 1) * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) + 1 ∧
        (∀ u < T,
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .done ∧
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .escape) := by
  let d := Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)
  let c := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out
  have hpos (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ d) : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length :=
    (Nat.add_le_add_left (Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 1) hr) j).trans hfit
  have horbit (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ d) :
      counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r =
        guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) (hpos r hr) out :=
    guardBlock_orbit b x j hj out r (hpos r hr)
  let T := (∑ r ∈ Finset.range d,
    guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r)) +
      counterOverhead w (d + 1)
  have hrun := counterLoopTM_run_done (guardBlockTM b) (guardPhase b 0) (some none)
    (guardTime b) c w (FinTM.bufferTape w) 0 (by intro p _ _; simp) d rfl
    (by
      intro r hr
      rw [horbit r (by omega), horbit (r + 1) (by omega)]
      obtain ⟨hs, ht, hi⟩ := guardBlock_segment b x _ (hpos r (by omega)) out
      refine ⟨hs, ht, ?_, rfl⟩
      intro u hu hut
      obtain ⟨s, hsu, hsa, hse⟩ := hi u hu hut
      exact ⟨s, hsu, hsa, fun he => hse (Option.some.inj he).symm⟩) T rfl
  have ht := counterLoop_time_le (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c w d rfl (b + 1)
    (fun _ _ => Nat.min_le_left _ _)
  have hd : d ≤ (b + 1) * d := by
    simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul_right d (show 1 ≤ b + 1 by omega)
  refine ⟨T, ?_, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [T]
    rw [Nat.mul_comm d (b + 1)] at ht
    dsimp [d] at ht hd ⊢
    omega
  · dsimp only
    have he : (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T = _ := hrun.1
    rw [he, horbit d le_rfl]
    exact ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, hrun.2.1⟩

/-- If the requested blocks do not fit, the physical guard reaches `escape`
in time independent of the value represented by the binary counter.

**Proof sketch.** Divide the available input length by the positive block
size. Exactly that many full body rounds fit, and the next round detects the
right blank. Apply the public escaping counter-host contract and its prefix
amortization bound; there are at most `|x| + 1` attempted rounds. -/
private lemma binaryGuard_escape (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out w : List Bool)
    (hshort : x.length < j + (b + 1) * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) :
    ∃ T ≤ (b + 5) * (x.length + 1) + 2 * w.length,
      let c := (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T
      c.state = some .escape ∧ c.output = out ∧ c.inputPos.val = x.length + 1 ∧
        (∀ u < T,
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .done ∧
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .escape) := by
  let r₀ := (x.length - j) / (b + 1)
  let c := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out
  have hdiv := Nat.mod_add_div (x.length - j) (b + 1)
  have hmod := Nat.mod_lt (x.length - j) (Nat.succ_pos b)
  have hstart : j + (b + 1) * r₀ ≤ x.length := by dsimp [r₀]; omega
  have hlast : x.length - (j + (b + 1) * r₀) < b + 1 := by
    rw [← Nat.sub_sub]
    change (x.length - j) - (b + 1) * ((x.length - j) / (b + 1)) < b + 1
    rw [← Nat.mod_eq_sub_mul_div]
    exact hmod
  have hr₀ : r₀ < Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) := by
    by_contra hn
    have hm := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 1) (Nat.le_of_not_gt hn)
    omega
  have hpos (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ r₀) : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length :=
    (Nat.add_le_add_left (Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 1) hr) j).trans hstart
  have horbit (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ r₀) :
      counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r =
        guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) (hpos r hr) out :=
    guardBlock_orbit b x j hj out r (hpos r hr)
  have hexit : counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c (r₀ + 1) =
      guardCfg b x none x.length le_rfl out := by
    change (fun z => (guardBlockTM b).runFrom z (guardTime b z))^[r₀ + 1] c = _
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    change (guardBlockTM b).runFrom
      (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r₀)
      (guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r₀)) = _
    rw [horbit r₀ le_rfl]
    have ht : guardTime b
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r₀) hstart out) =
        x.length - (j + (b + 1) * r₀) + 1 := by
      dsimp [guardTime, guardCfg]
      omega
    rw [ht]
    exact guardBlock_short b x _ hstart hlast out
  let T := (∑ r ∈ Finset.range (r₀ + 1),
    guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r)) +
      counterOverhead w (r₀ + 1)
  have hrun := counterLoopTM_run_escape (guardBlockTM b) (guardPhase b 0) none
    (by simp [guardPhase]) (guardTime b) c w (FinTM.bufferTape w) 0
    (by intro p _ _; simp) r₀ hr₀ (by
      intro r hr
      rw [horbit r hr]
      exact guardBlock_segment b x _ (hpos r hr) out)
    (by rw [hexit]; rfl) T rfl
  have hs : (∑ r ∈ Finset.range (r₀ + 1),
      guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r)) ≤
        (r₀ + 1) * (b + 1) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ _r ∈ Finset.range (r₀ + 1), (b + 1) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum (fun _ _ => Nat.min_le_left _ _)
      _ = _ := by simp
  have hc := counterOverhead_le_of_le w (r₀ + 1) (by omega)
  have hn : r₀ + 1 ≤ x.length + 1 := by
    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right r₀ (show 1 ≤ b + 1 by omega)
    simp only [one_mul] at this
    omega
  refine ⟨T, ?_, ?_⟩
  · calc
      T ≤ (r₀ + 1) * (b + 1) + (4 * (r₀ + 1) + 2 * w.length) :=
        Nat.add_le_add hs hc
      _ = (b + 5) * (r₀ + 1) + 2 * w.length := by ring
      _ ≤ _ := Nat.add_le_add_right (Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 5) hn) _
  · dsimp only
    have he : (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T = _ := hrun.1
    rw [he, hexit]
    exact ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, hrun.2.1⟩



/-- The last bit, with the empty word accepted as canonical zero. -/
private def canonBitsOK (w : List Bool) : Bool := w.getLast?.getD true

/-- A last-symbol fold has exactly the finite scan's canonicality verdict. -/
private lemma canonBits_fold (w : List Bool) (a : Bool) :
    w.foldl (fun _ b => b) a = w.getLast?.getD a := by
  induction w generalizing a with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih =>
    simp only [List.foldl_cons, ih, List.getLast?_cons, Option.getD_some]

/-- A finite last-bit check suffices to recover the canonical binary word.

**Proof sketch.** Remove the low bit. A nonempty canonical tail has positive
value, so adjoining either low bit is exactly the binary constructor law;
the singleton case admits only the bit one. -/
private lemma canonBits_of_last (w : List Bool) :
    canonBitsOK w = true → (w.foldr Nat.bit 0).bits = w := by
  induction w with
  | nil => intro _; simp
  | cons b w ih =>
    intro h
    cases w with
    | nil => cases b <;> simp_all [canonBitsOK, Nat.bit]
    | cons c w =>
      have htail : canonBitsOK (c :: w) = true := by
        simpa only [canonBitsOK, List.getLast?_cons_cons] using h
      have he := ih htail
      have hne : (c :: w).foldr Nat.bit 0 ≠ 0 := by
        intro hz
        simp only [hz, Nat.zero_bits] at he
        contradiction
      rw [List.foldr_cons, Nat.bits_append_bit _ b (fun hz => (hne hz).elim), he]

/-- Canonical natural-number digits pass the finite last-bit check.

**Proof sketch.** Use the public binary recursion from zero and one, so every
extension has a nonzero tail. The public decoding identity shows that such
a tail has nonempty digits; its last bit is unchanged by the extension. -/
private lemma canonBits_bits (n : ℕ) : canonBitsOK n.bits = true := by
  refine Nat.binaryRecFromOne (motive := fun m => canonBitsOK m.bits = true)
    (by simp [canonBitsOK]) (by simp [canonBitsOK]) ?_ n
  intro low tail nonzero canonical
  have nonempty : tail.bits ≠ [] := by
    intro hempty
    have decoded := codeBitsNat_bits tail
    rw [hempty] at decoded
    exact nonzero decoded.symm
  rw [Nat.bits_append_bit tail low (fun hz => (nonzero hz).elim)]
  cases htail : tail.bits with
  | nil => exact (nonempty htail).elim
  | cons first rest =>
    simpa only [canonBitsOK, htail, List.getLast?_cons_cons] using canonical

/-- The finite check recognizes exactly the canonical little-endian words. -/
private lemma canonBitsOK_iff (w : List Bool) :
    canonBitsOK w = true ↔ w = (w.foldr Nat.bit 0).bits := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (canonBits_of_last w h).symm
  · intro h
    calc
      canonBitsOK w = canonBitsOK (w.foldr Nat.bit 0).bits := congrArg canonBitsOK h
      _ = true := canonBits_bits _

/-- A spare high zero makes the state-count successor nonoverflowing. -/
private def canonCount (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (incFixed (w ++ [false])).getD []

/-- Incrementing with a spare high zero preserves the enlarged width and
represents one more than the original header, including the empty header.

**Proof sketch.** Follow the carry through the low one bits. At the first
zero the increment stops; the appended zero guarantees that this happens.
Each recursive carry doubles the value equation. -/
private lemma canonCount_spec (w : List Bool) :
    incFixed (w ++ [false]) = some (canonCount w) ∧
      (canonCount w).length = w.length + 1 ∧
      (canonCount w).foldr Nat.bit 0 = w.foldr Nat.bit 0 + 1 := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [canonCount, incFixed, Nat.bit]
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b with
    | false =>
      simp [canonCount, incFixed, List.foldr_append, Nat.bit]
    | true =>
      have he : canonCount (true :: w) = false :: canonCount w := by
        change ((incFixed (w ++ [false])).map (false :: ·)).getD [] = _
        rw [ih.1]
        rfl
      rw [he]
      simp only [List.cons_append, incFixed, ih.1, Option.map_some,
        List.length_cons, ih.2.1, List.foldr_cons, ih.2.2, Nat.bit]
      simp [Nat.mul_add, Nat.add_assoc]

/-- The canonical-bit checker is the public two-pass scan, with the last
symbol as accumulator and an identity return pass. -/
private def canonBitsTM (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Bool (ScanPhase Bool) :=
  scanTM k i (scanFold (fun _ b => b)) scanKeep true

/-- The canonicality scan preserves every seam word, the native input
position and the empty output, and avoids both verdict anchors until its
exact linear-time return.

**Proof sketch.** Specialize the public scan contract to the last-bit fold.
Its pure result preserves the scanned word, so the interval rewrite is the
original buffer at every cell. The shared contract supplies both exit cuts. -/
private lemma canonBitsTM_run (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (α : List Bool)
    (w : Fin k → List Bool) :
    (canonBitsTM k i).runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (.fwd true) w)
        (2 * (w i).length + 2) = Cfg.ofWords (.done (canonBitsOK (w i))) w ∧
      (∀ t < 2 * (w i).length + 2, ∀ b,
        ((canonBitsTM k i).runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (.fwd true) w) t).state ≠
          some (.done b)) := by
  let d := Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (ScanPhase.fwd true) w
  have h := scanTM_run_ofCfg i (scanFold (fun (_ : Bool) b => b)) scanKeep true
    (w i) d rfl (by intro p _ _; simp [d, Cfg.ofWords])
  rw [scanResult_fold, canonBits_fold] at h
  refine ⟨h.1.trans ?_, h.2.1⟩
  apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
  funext j z
  dsimp only [d, Cfg.ofWords]
  split_ifs with hz
  · rcases hz with ⟨rfl, _, _⟩
    simp
  · rfl

/-- A strict first-return form of the inherited physical header call, ready
for the public seam combinator even when the original anchors coincide.

**Proof sketch.** If the original anchors differ, time zero is excluded by
that inequality. If they coincide, apply the public release adapter, whose
fresh entry executes the call before any return can be dispatched. The
machine and all tape/output data are otherwise those of the inherited call. -/
private lemma exists_canonHeaderSeam :
    ∃ (C : FinTM Bool) (entry exit : C.State) (a : ℕ), 0 < C.k ∧
      ∀ α : List Bool, ∃ t ≤ a * (α.length + 1), 0 < t ∧
        (∀ u < t,
          (C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) entry (fun _ => [])) u).state ≠
            some exit) ∧
        C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) entry (fun _ => [])) t =
          Cfg.ofWords exit (stateWord C.k (canonHeader α)) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨C, entry, exit, a, hk, hC⟩ := exists_canonHeaderCall
  by_cases he : entry = exit
  · subst exit
    let R : FinTM Bool := {
      k := C.k
      State := Unit ⊕ C.State
      tm := seamReleaseTM C.tm entry }
    refine ⟨R, Sum.inl (), Sum.inr entry, a, hk, ?_⟩
    intro α
    obtain ⟨t, ht, hpos, hcut, hrun⟩ := hC α
    have hr := seamReleaseTM_firstReturn C.tm entry rfl hpos hrun rfl hcut
    refine ⟨t, ht, hpos, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [R, Cfg.ofWords, Cfg.mapState, Option.map_some] using hr.2
    · simpa only [R, Cfg.ofWords, Cfg.mapState, Option.map_some] using hr.1
  · refine ⟨C, entry, exit, a, hk, ?_⟩
    intro α
    obtain ⟨t, ht, hpos, hcut, hrun⟩ := hC α
    refine ⟨t, ht, hpos, ?_, hrun⟩
    intro u hu
    by_cases hz : u = 0
    · subst u
      change some entry ≠ some exit
      exact fun h => he (Option.some.inj h)
    · exact hcut u (by omega) hu

/-- The nonoverflowing count word is computed in linear time by two public
primitives: append a zero, then increment at that fixed width.

**Proof sketch.** Compose the append-bit and fixed-width increment machines.
Their linear budgets compose to a linear budget; the added constant is
absorbed using the positive input-length offset. -/
private lemma exists_canonCountTM :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (a : ℕ),
      M.ComputesFunInTime canonCount (fun n => a * (n + 1)) := by
  obtain ⟨A, a, hA⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_appendBit false
  obtain ⟨B, b, hB⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_incFixed
  obtain ⟨M, c, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp hA hB
    (fun _ _ h => Nat.mul_le_mul_left b (by omega))
  refine ⟨M, c * (a + b * (a + 1) + 1), ?_⟩
  intro w
  apply (hM w).mono
  calc
    c * (a * (w.length + 1) + b * (a * (w.length + 1) + 1) + 1) ≤
        c * ((a * (w.length + 1) + b * (a * (w.length + 1) + 1) + 1) +
          (b + 1) * w.length) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (Nat.le_add_right _ _)
    _ = _ := by ring

/-- Emit the scan's verdict on its final transition. All scanning transitions
are the existing public scan; only its live exits receive a halting action. -/
private def canonVerdictTM (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Bool (ScanPhase Bool) where
  q₀ := .fwd true
  tr := fun q inp work => match q with
    | .done b => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), some b, none⟩
    | _ => (canonBitsTM k i).tr q inp work

/-- From a loaded word, the verdict wrapper halts with exactly its canonicality
bit after the public scan and one emitting transition.

**Proof sketch.** The scan avoids both verdict states until its return. Apply
the public guarded-agreement transfer on those states, then execute the one
new halting action. No scan trace is re-proved. -/
private lemma canonVerdictTM_run (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (α : List Bool)
    (w : Fin k → List Bool) :
    let c := (canonVerdictTM k i).runFrom
      (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (.fwd true) w) (2 * (w i).length + 3)
    c.state = none ∧ c.output = [canonBitsOK (w i)] := by
  obtain ⟨hscan, hcut⟩ := canonBitsTM_run k i α w
  have hid : ⇑(Function.Embedding.refl (ScanPhase Bool)) = id := rfl
  have hpre := MultiTapeTM.runFrom_mapState_of_agreeOn
    (canonBitsTM k i) (canonVerdictTM k i) (Function.Embedding.refl _)
    (fun q => ∀ b, q ≠ ScanPhase.done b)
    (by
      intro q hq inp work
      simp only [hid, id_eq]
      cases q with
      | fwd a => simp [canonVerdictTM, Action.mapState]
      | bwd a => simp [canonVerdictTM, Action.mapState]
      | done b => exact (hq b rfl).elim)
    (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (.fwd true) w) (2 * (w i).length + 2)
    (by
      intro u hu q hq b he
      exact hcut u hu b (hq.trans (congrArg some he)))
  simp only [hid, Cfg.mapState, Option.map_id, id_eq] at hpre
  change ((canonVerdictTM k i).runFrom _ ((2 * (w i).length + 2) + 1)).state = none ∧ _
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', hpre, hscan]
  simp [MultiTapeTM.step, Cfg.ofWords, canonVerdictTM, Action.apply]


/-- The loaded-header scan, reached through the inherited native-input call,
computes the canonicality bit in linear time.

**Proof sketch.** Use the strict loader seam, then the public scan with its
single emitting exit. The loader restores the native input and clean work
heads. Its returned header has length at most the input length, so the two
linear ledgers and the one dispatch step have a common linear bound. -/
private lemma exists_canonHeaderBitsTM :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (a : ℕ),
      M.ComputesFunInTime (fun α => [canonBitsOK (canonHeader α)])
        (fun n => a * (n + 1)) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨C, entry, exit, a, hk, hC⟩ := exists_canonHeaderSeam
  let i : Fin C.k := ⟨0, hk⟩
  let V := canonVerdictTM C.k i
  let L := seamCompTM C.tm exit V (ScanPhase.fwd true)
  let M : FinTM Bool := {
    k := C.k
    State := C.State ⊕ ScanPhase Bool
    tm := { L with q₀ := Sum.inl entry } }
  refine ⟨M, a + 4, ?_⟩
  intro α
  obtain ⟨t, ht, _, hcut, hload⟩ := hC α
  let w := stateWord C.k (canonHeader α)
  have hw : w i = canonHeader α := by simp [w, stateWord, i]
  let v := V.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (.fwd true) w)
    (2 * (w i).length + 3)
  have hv : v.state = none ∧ v.output = [canonBitsOK (w i)] :=
    canonVerdictTM_run C.k i α w
  have hrun := seamCompTM_run_ofCfg C.tm exit V (.fwd true)
    (c₃ := v) hload rfl hcut (by
      simp only [Cfg.ofWords, Cfg.mapState, Option.map_some]
      rfl)
  have hinit : M.tm.initCfg α =
      (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) entry (fun _ => [])).mapState Sum.inl := by
    simp [M, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init, Cfg.ofWords, Cfg.mapState,
      FinTM.bufferTape_nil]
  have hbase : M.ComputesInTime α [canonBitsOK (canonHeader α)]
      (t + 1 + (2 * (w i).length + 3)) := by
    apply (FinTM.computesInTime_iff M _ _ _).mpr
    rw [hinit]
    change (L.runFrom _ _).state = none ∧ (L.runFrom _ _).output = _
    rw [hrun]
    simpa only [Cfg.mapState, hv.1, Option.map_none, hw] using hv
  apply hbase.mono
  have hlen := canonHeader_length α
  rw [hw]
  calc
    t + 1 + (2 * (canonHeader α).length + 3) ≤
        a * (α.length + 1) + 2 * α.length + 4 := by omega
    _ ≤ (a + 4) * (α.length + 1) := by
      rw [Nat.add_mul]
      omega

/-- Header validity keeps pair-grammar failure separate from the loader's
empty-word fallback; a successfully decoded empty header is canonical zero. -/
private def canonHeaderOK (α : List Bool) : Bool :=
  (pairDecode α).isSome && canonBitsOK (canonHeader α)

/-- The physical header predicate tests precisely successful pair decoding
and canonical binary state-count digits. -/
private lemma canonHeaderOK_iff (α : List Bool) :
    canonHeaderOK α = true ↔
      ∃ bits rest, pairDecode α = some (bits, rest) ∧ bits = (codeBitsNat bits).bits := by
  cases hp : pairDecode α with
  | none => simp [canonHeaderOK, hp]
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨bits, rest⟩
    simp [canonHeaderOK, canonHeader, hp, canonBitsOK_iff, codeBitsNat]

/-- Header rejection is a genuine scanner failure, never an accidental
acceptance of the loader's default empty word.

**Proof sketch.** Pair failure is the scanner's first failure. For a decoded
pair, failure of the last-bit test is equivalent to failure of the scanner's
canonical-binary equality. -/
private lemma scan_eq_none_of_canonHeaderOK (F : MachineFormat) (α : List Bool)
    (h : canonHeaderOK α = false) : F.scan α = none := by
  cases hp : pairDecode α with
  | none => simp [CodeFormat.scan, hp]
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨bits, rest⟩
    have hb : bits ≠ (codeBitsNat bits).bits := by
      intro he
      have ht : canonHeaderOK α = true :=
        (canonHeaderOK_iff α).mpr ⟨bits, rest, hp, he⟩
      simp [h] at ht
    simp [CodeFormat.scan, hp, hb]

/-- A total linear-time validator checks pair success separately and runs the
loaded-header checker only on successful pairs.
```
